children: Turkey’s trade deficit widened to $5.24 billion in August 2026 from $4.28 billion in the same month a year earlier, according to preliminary data.
Imports rose 10.5% year-on-year to $28.7 billion, mainly from China ($4.7 billion), Germany ($2.1 billion), and the US ($1.9 billion).
By sector, imports were mainly from the manufacturing industry (82.4%), mining and quarrying (12%), and agriculture, forestry and fishing (2.9%).
Meanwhile, exports increased 8.1% to $23.5 billion, with Germany as the top export destination ($1.8 billion), followed by the US ($1.7 billion) and the UK ($1.2 billion).
By sector, exports were dominated by the manufacturing industry (93.5%), agriculture, forestry and fishing (3.2%), and mining and quarrying (2.3%).
During January-August, the country’s cumulative trade deficit reached $57.4 billion, with exports rising 4% to $185 billion and imports increasing 5.3% to $250.8 billion.

title: Turkey Trade Deficit Widens in August
